records.rule: Restart recovery persists LDAP application authority facts through IdentityPeerAuthorityJournal and IdentityPeerAuthoritySnapshot.
Recovered authority epoch may advance but may not regress.
Within the same authority epoch, a different holder is rejected. Holder transfer requires a newer epoch.
XTP transport ACK or replay evidence cannot satisfy LDAP application-commit authority.
Instrumentation Mesh correlation and causation are evidence only; they do not imply directory commit or failover authority.
Logical peer identity survives runtime replacement and carrier change; physical node identity is not the semantic peer.
One authoritative DirectoryChange has one peer-update request identity independent of target count; replication is not consensus.
Durable recovery retries only targets lacking application ACK evidence.
oorexxEntityId is platform semantic identity; entryUUID is LDAP entry identity; DN is an address.
LDAP Bind attribution is not authorization and not exact object-method permission.
Directory commit is write-before-memory; durable append failure must not advance in-memory truth.
Persistent credential records carry secretRef and never raw secret values.
Native LDAP schema enforcement is an LDAP-personality concern and does not move semantic authority out of Identity Directory.
